items.title: GPU map renderer: smooth pan and zoom, no visible redraws
Lot-based towns: streets, sidewalks, invisible slot grid; towns start small and grow
Painting pipeline: engine guides → ChatGPT → 30° tilt check → atlas packing
Build flow: pick a look, choose a highlighted site, construction rises over the build time
Core building set: houses, shops, civic, industry, parks (lots v1–v3)
10 painted resource deposits, clickable across their ground
135 product pictures in the facility panels
No repeated design within a block; every lot gets art that fits it
Front-row buildings face their street
Lane-true traffic with period vehicles that change with the years
13 new animated vehicle sheets; frames aligned so bodies never hop
Motor vehicles drive steadily (no shimmer); horse carts walk
Factory smoke leaves the painted chimney tops
Animated water: fountains, lake and pond ripples and glints
Animated clock hands on clock towers
items.detail: Moving hands on 4 clock faces (two city halls, belfry, Victorian town hall); re-detect after the roof repaints are packed, and teach the detector the smaller shop and post-office clocks.

items.title: Ateshgah fire temple: animated flames and a warm glow on its fire altars (owner, 2026-10-16)
All new paintings get roofs that read correctly from the map camera
Repaint 8 flagged buildings (courthouse, post office, bank, police, Art Nouveau store, hotel, apartment block, Deco civic centre without French flags)
Repaint 16 houses and shops whose low roofs look folded backwards
Glass-box check: every painting must fill its own layout box (footprint, walls and height)
Repaint the buildings that ignored their box (department store, New York and London shops and houses, their rear views)
Each city's own architecture (New York, London, Baku, Tokyo, Emerald Coast, Ironforge)
Later eras: 1920s Deco to 1950s towers
Towns redevelop lot by lot over the decades
Roads of their time: setts in towns, gravel country roads, tarmac in the 1920s, asphalt in the 1930s; farm tracks stay dirt
Real-building pipeline: owner photos → glass-box layout → ChatGPT painting in the game style
Baku landmark: the twin-domed clock building beside Winter Park, from the owner's photos, as Baku's city hall
Landmarks that change with the years: Baku's site shows the 1908 Hajinski house early on and the twin-domed building later (one extra painting, from the owner's photos)
Real landmarks for every city, from the owner's photos (Baku first, then the other five)
Every new map places each city's landmarks around its centre
Players can build landmarks as wonders: very expensive (proposal ~$100M), unlocked at ~$100–150M yearly capitalisation with the cash, or funded over time from the budget
AI rivals start rich, so they cannot rush wonders: same unlock rules, no wonders at game start
Wonders draw visitors: more street life and traffic, and more customers for nearby shops (effect sizes as a proposal for sign-off)
Baku Old City walls with gates (Double Gates) where streets pass into the new town (owner, 2026-10-16)
Rear views for big stores and banks built on a back site, so the entrance faces its street
Construction-site paintings (groundworks and scaffolded frame per lot size)
Show the construction-site paintings while buildings go up
Leafier towns: trees in yards and between buildings
Denser, taller city cores
Factory art matches the product made
Vacant lots look intentional, not bare lawn squares
Parked lorries at factory loading bays
Fix the long-failing city-plan regression check
Bring the new map into the main game (owner sign-off)
items.detail: Owner approved the merge plan (docs/MERGE_PLAN.md) on 2026-10-15. Lab prep done: art as WebP (123 MB to 27 MB), light detail for phones (16 MB download, about 110 MB of graphics memory), tour and objectives checklist fixed for the new screen, economic map window repaired, and each facility's site saved for v0.30 location economics. All 18 map tests pass. Next: review tonight's art run, then copy into the main game step by step.

items.title: Location matters: where a building stands changes its freight, land price and walk-in customers (rivals follow the same rules)
Baku's oil fields sit at the edge of town, as the real Bibi-Heybat and Balakhany fields did
